paper.title_en: Flat "Island of Stability" of Superheavy Nuclei
paper.abstract_en: We present the first systematic microscopic calculations of fission barrier heights for 292 even-even superheavy nuclei using the multidimensionally constrained relativistic mean field model with triaxial and octupole deformations treated simultaneously. The calculated barrier heights remain around 5 MeV in the vicinity of the predicted doubly magic nucleus ${}^{304}120$. This flat landscape contrasts with the conventional picture of mutually enhanced magicity and indicates that the proton shell closure at $Z=120$ and the neutron shell closure at $N=184$ do not reinforce but suppress each other. We introduce an $α$-linked energy difference $Δ_{\rm pn}$ to identify the mutually suppressed magicity caused by distinct proton and neutron density distributions. These results challenge the expected shell landscape of superheavy nuclei and may have a crucial impact on estimating survival probabilities in the synthesis of superheavy nuclei.
